rows.label: Concept
rows.text: Mendelian inheritance tracks alleles. They segregate, one to each gamete, giving 1:2:1 genotypes and 3:1 phenotypes under complete dominance. Unlinked genes assort independently and give 9:3:3:1. A test cross uncovers a hidden recessive allele.

rows.label: Formula
rows.text:
A gene can exist as alleles. A diploid individual carries two alleles of each gene.
Dominance means that in a heterozygote, one allele's phenotype hides the other allele's phenotype.

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: 3:1 is phenotype. 1:2:1 is genotype under complete dominance.  ·  Assortment is for different genes. Segregation is for the two alleles of one gene.

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: Mendel worked with pea plants but his laws apply to all sexually reproducing organisms.  ·  The concept of incomplete dominance (e.g., flower color in snapdragons) deviates from classical Mendelian ratios.

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: Segregation: those two alleles separate when gametes form, so each gamete gets one.

rows.label: Limitation
rows.text: Stay inside this class 11 topic.  ·  Do not add an unsupported count.

rows.label: Derivation
rows.text: Write the table.  ·  Add one trap.

rows.label: Shortcut
rows.text: 3:1 ratio in monohybrid cross = dominant:recessive phenotype.  ·  Punnett square predicts 25% AA, 50% Aa, 25% aa in Aa × Aa cross.

rows.label: Board question
rows.text: In a cross between Aa and aa, what are the expected genotypes and phenotypes?  ·  Draw a Punnett square for a monohybrid cross (Aa × Aa).

rows.label: Hints
rows.text: Be careful with terminology: genotype = genetic makeup, phenotype = observable traits.  ·  Use Punnett squares for dihybrid crosses (9:3:3:1 ratio for independent assortment).

rows.label: Quick concepts
rows.text: Mendelian inheritance: traits follow predictable patterns  ·  Dominant and recessive alleles  ·  Heterozygous (Aa) and homozygous (AA, aa) genotypes  ·  Phenotype vs genotype

rows.label: Key points
rows.text: Mendelian ratios: 3:1 for dominant/recessive in monohybrid crosses.  ·  Punnett squares are essential for predicting offspring genotypes and phenotypes.  ·  Dominant traits appear in the phenotype even when recessive allele is present (heterozygous).  ·  Recessive traits only appear in homozygous recessive individuals (aa).

rows.label: More practice
rows.text: Explain why a heterozygous individual (Aa) shows the dominant phenotype.  ·  What is incomplete dominance and give an example?

rows.label: More hints
rows.text: Mendel's laws apply to autosomal traits; sex-linked traits require different analysis.

rows.label: MCQ drill

rows.label: Study notes
rows.text: A cross of two heterozygotes therefore gives a genotype ratio of 1:2:1 and, if dominance is complete, a phenotype ratio of 3:1.  ·  Independent assortment: alleles of different, unlinked genes are sorted independently. Two such genes in a double heterozygote cross give 9:3:3:1.  ·  A test cross with the homozygous recessive reveals whether a dominant phenotype hides a recessive allele. Linked genes are the exception this note only flags: they do not assort independently.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Punnett square: a method for predicting offspring genotypes  ·  A test cross is not a cross of two unknowns.  ·  Linked genes break the 9:3:3:1 expectation.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Sex-linked inheritance (X-linked traits) follows a different pattern due to sex chromosomes.  ·  Order in a sequence is part of the answer.  ·  Do not call a timberline a snowline.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: In a monohybrid cross (Aa × Aa), the genotypic ratio is 1:2:1 (AA:Aa:aa) and the phenotypic ratio is 3:1 (dominant:recessive).  ·  Dominant alleles mask recessive alleles in heterozygous individuals.  ·  Mendel's law of segregation states that alleles separate during gamete formation.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Dominant allele masks recessive allele in heterozygotes (Aa looks like AA).  ·  Give the character and one example.  ·  State the contrast.
